rationale: Start with a broad, moderately fast scouting gradient to locate all eight peaks and identify critical pairs while limiting late-elution risk. The midpoint temperature leaves room to test temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Keep the gradient fixed and raise temperature to test selectivity changes in the crowded middle cluster and late doublet. The short initial elution window provides ample room for subsequent gradient shallowing if needed.

Use a substantially shallower gradient at the better-performing temperature to spread the three unresolved pairs and test slope-dependent selectivity. The strong final solvent should still elute all compounds, while the current short retention window allows this slower gradient.

Shorten the promising shallow gradient to bring the last peak closer to 10 minutes and remove the time penalty. This also tests whether the marginal pair improves or deteriorates with a modest slope increase.

The critical pair nearly coelutes at 20 minutes, suggesting a selectivity crossover rather than simple loss of separation. Test a faster gradient on the opposite side of that crossover, aiming to recover its resolution while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

The best method is almost fully resolved, but increasing slope risks the middle pair already at R = 1.55. Test a small temperature decrease at the same gradient to shift selectivity and potentially resolve the remaining pair without sacrificing that separation.

Return to 60 C and test a higher starting organic fraction with a slightly shallower slope. This changes gradient selectivity beyond simple slope adjustment, seeking to resolve the remaining pair while preserving the middle separation and sub-10-minute elution.

Slightly steepen injection 7 by raising the final organic fraction one grid step. This should improve its remaining critical pair while retaining enough resolution in the middle cluster, with the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

This gives a slope of 0.045 organic fraction/min, just above injection 8’s 0.04444, targeting the R = 1.49 pair without exhausting the middle pairs’ small margins. All peaks should elute before the gradient ends, so the lower endpoint should preserve the relevant gradient profile.

Injection 9 has reached the maximum CRF and remains the benchmark. Raise both solvent endpoints one step to preserve slope while testing a shorter elution window; the narrow resolution margins will reveal whether this time reduction is feasible.

Keep injection 9 as the maximum-score benchmark and slightly flatten the faster, higher-starting-organic method to recover its middle-cluster resolution. This tests whether the shorter elution window can be retained without pushing the later pairs below R = 1.5.

Return to the fully resolved starting composition and increase the gradient slope only slightly, from 0.045 to 0.04583 organic fraction/min. This probes the shortest-method boundary near injection 9 while retaining that maximum-CRF method as the fallback.

The local slope boundary is now bracketed, with injection 9 retaining the maximum score. Test the low-temperature selectivity regime with the original fast scouting gradient to look for a different route to complete resolution in a shorter elution window.

The low-temperature scout separates most pairs well in a short window. Make the gradient moderately shallower to test whether both remaining pairs can reach R = 1.5 while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test a shallower gradient beyond the low-temperature middle-pair crossover, using a higher starting organic fraction to offset the added retention time. Injection 9 remains the maximum-score fallback while this probes an alternative fully resolved window.

Further flatten the low-temperature gradient to move the remaining middle pair away from its crossover, with all other pairs already resolved. The last peak should remain near or below 10 minutes, offering another potential maximum-score method.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to shorten the newly resolved low-temperature method. Keeping the duration fixed also slightly reduces slope, which may help preserve its marginal middle-pair resolution.

The higher starting fraction shifted the low-temperature middle pair back toward its crossover. Test farther on the opposite side with a higher start and moderately steeper slope, seeking a shorter resolved method while retaining injection 9 as the maximum-score benchmark.

Injection 18 achieves maximum CRF with a much shorter elution window and useful resolution margins. Shorten its gradient one step to test a further time reduction while monitoring the late doublet and middle cluster.

Shorten the gradient another grid step to locate the full-resolution boundary. Injection 19 is the fastest fully resolved method so far and remains the fallback if either marginal pair drops below R = 1.5.

The slope-only speed limit lies between injections 19 and 20. Test a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient to shorten retention while compensating for compression of the critical pairs.

Return to the fastest fully resolved gradient and raise temperature one step to test a further retention-time reduction through temperature-dependent selectivity. Injection 19 remains the fallback if either critical pair loses full resolution.

The small temperature increase moved the critical middle pair toward coelution. Test a larger increase to seek separation beyond that crossover and a shorter elution window, retaining injection 19 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Return to the fastest fully resolved region and test a slope halfway between injections 19 and 20. This refines the speed–resolution boundary, with injection 19 retained if the middle pair falls below R = 1.5.

Use injection 19’s fully resolved slope but end the programmed gradient at 4 minutes; its outlet endpoint at 4.65 minutes remains after the observed last peak at 4.14 minutes. This should preserve maximum CRF while substantially shortening the programmed gradient, with injection 19 retained as the confirmed benchmark.
